# hiok_public_ip (Resource)

A public IP address allocated from the region's routed prefix and configured on the host so it reaches a container or virtual machine.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `family` (Number) 4 or 6. Only IPv6 is assignable today: a region's IPv4 is a single provider address and it is the host's own, so there is nothing to hand out.
- `hostname` (String) Publish DNS for the address under this name. A bare label lands in the managed zone; a fully-qualified name is used as given.
- `region` (String) Region whose pool the address comes from. Defaults to the provider's first region.
- `resource_id` (String) Identifier of the resource holding the address.
- `resource_kind` (String) What holds the address: virtualmachine, container, bastion, …
- `resource_name` (String) Display name of the resource holding the address.
- `set_reverse_dns` (Boolean) Publish reverse DNS as well as the forward record. The provider forward-confirms, so this can only succeed once the forward record is live.
- `target_kind` (String) "container" or "vm". A container is configured by entering its namespace; a VM is reached through its guest agent, so they are not interchangeable.
- `target_name` (String) The name the HOST knows the guest by: the Docker container name, or the libvirt domain (which for a VM is "<guid>#<name>"). Leave empty to reserve the address without configuring any host.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) The allocated address.
- `configured` (Boolean) True once the host actually carries the route and NDP proxy entry.
- `gateway` (String) Upstream gateway for the pool.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `prefix_length` (Number) Prefix length of the guest's address.
- `ptr_status` (String) Why reverse DNS was not published, when it was not.
- `status_message` (String) Why the address is not fully configured, when it is not. A VM whose image has no QEMU guest agent gets the host half only, and says so here.
